correctness.rationale: For k=3, whether an index admits a block length at most 6 is determined by its length-18 factor; for k=4 and block length at most 10, by its length-40 factor. Garg explicitly uses the fact that the Fibonacci word is Sturmian, so it has exactly N+1 distinct factors of length N. The package exhibits 19 distinct length-18 factors and 41 distinct length-40 factors from the fixed point, hence exhausts both factor sets. Every block partition is then checked exactly. Four length-18 factors require 6 for k=3, and one length-40 factor requires 10 for k=4, providing matching lower bounds.

originality.rationale: The direct paper proves a global linear upper bound for all k and defines the pointwise minimum gamma_i(k), but the inspected full text states asymptotic bounds rather than exact small-k uniform maxima. Berger--Defant supply the general conjectural framework and later-update context, not the values 6 and 10. Five targeted published-finding corpus searches and several web searches found no statement implying these two exact radii.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, note, or computation may contain the same two values under different notation.
The claim intentionally does not extend beyond k=4; larger exact radii may exhibit additional structure.
The finite factor certificate depends on the standard published Sturmian complexity fact for the Fibonacci word; it does not independently reprove Sturmianity.

value.rationale: The direct literature singles out the Fibonacci word as the first non-uniform morphic example with a uniform linear antipower bound and explicitly studies the pointwise minimum gamma_i(k). Since k=2 is trivial, k=3 and k=4 are the first two nontrivial uniform radii. Determining them exactly supplies sharp base cases for the central quantitative invariant rather than an arbitrary prefix-length computation, and the unique k=4 extremal factor gives a concrete structural obstruction benchmark for future work.
